T0647.title: Proxy Sniping
T0647.definition: Proxy sniping is a black-market or scalper service that captures scarce tickets, appointment slots, or platform benefits for others using human, automated, or hybrid methods.
T0647.description:
Proxy sniping appears in scarce-resource scenarios such as concert tickets, popular attraction reservations, medical appointments, transport seats, limited products, and platform benefit claims. Service providers earn commissions or markups and use real-user accounts, bulk accounts, automation scripts, proxy IPs, SMS receiving platforms, or remotely controlled devices to submit requests at the moment of release.

In the BREAK knowledge base, proxy sniping is an upstream and downstream term around ticket scalping, unfair resource capture, and automated resale. It is not the same as ordinary purchasing assistance; the key distinction is whether it monetizes scaled capture, purchase-limit bypass, or disruption of fair allocation.
T0647.usageExample: Before ticket release, scalpers solicited proxy sniping orders in chat groups and promised to charge a service fee on top of the face value after success.
